event: VXE-845 auto aborted during launch climb with a VTOL error after GPS position accuracy exceeded the abort threshold, and returned to the ground without a crash.
failure_mode: GPS accuracy degraded past the launch abort threshold, triggering the designed abort
contributing: possible RF interference in the area (spectrum scan, not GNSS band)
unit operated radios on unallocated frequencies and bandwidths

evidence.quote: Exceeded accuracy thresholds during launch.

evidence.file: data/vxep/VXEP-1906/attachments/63402_AIR PMO Multiple Vehicle Investigation Report_20260709.pdf.md
evidence.quote: Logs display loss of GPS, aircraft then executed performed abort logic after loss of GPS and returned to ground.
There was very little time to operate the analyzer, and no GNSS-band analysis was performed to my knowledge.
Aircraft performed as expected.

would_settle_it.what: GPS accuracy and satellite count against the abort threshold at the abort time
GNSS jamming or C/N0 indicators to show whether the GPS loss was interference or sky view

would_settle_it.file: GNSS-band spectrum survey of the launch site
would_settle_it.what: evidence of interference in the GNSS bands at the site

reasoning: The engineer reviewing the AAR found the GPS accuracy threshold was exceeded during launch, and the multi-vehicle report says the logs show loss of GPS followed by the designed abort. The abort worked as designed on a degraded GPS input, so this is scored on GPS. Why GPS degraded is not shown: the report blames frequency and RF issues, but its findings are about Silvus radio frequency contention and no GNSS-band scan was done.
notes: Executive Summary says it was a training issue with wrong frequencies; the attached report's frequency findings concern the Silvus datalink at 2210/2280 MHz, not GNSS, so the link from wrong radio frequencies to GPS loss is not shown. The report also covers VXE 958, 721, 640 and 869 (PLZ overshoot, flyaways).

event: VXE 850 had a VTOL auto abort at about 100 ft on landing, then repeatedly flew through the transition point, ignored land immediately, lost comms in a bank and crashed into a river; aircraft never recovered.
contributing: no ELZ set by the operators
repeated VTOL landing attempts after an autopilot abort instead of a glide landing
loss of comms during a bank

evidence.quote: Each time it would blow through the transition point after IP5 with no errors or pop-ups.
The plane did not acknowledge the land immediately command.
No AIRFRAFT OR DATA
Operators did not set an ELZ to recover vehicle

team_root_cause:
Unable to identify because aircraft has not been recovered

Operators did not set an ELZ to recover vehicle

would_settle_it.what: recover the aircraft and its VTOL/XCOMM logs to find why the VTOL landing aborted and transitions were refused

would_settle_it.file: GCS AAR and logs from the VXE 850 flight
would_settle_it.what: abort reason codes and the command and link history before the loss

reasoning: The ticket describes an initial VTOL auto abort, then the aircraft refusing to transition again and ignoring land immediately, ending in a crash after a loss of comms. No aircraft or data were ever recovered, so nothing points to the cause of the first abort or the refused transitions. The missing ELZ is a contributing operator factor in the loss, not the cause of the abort.
notes: Team Root Cause says the cause could not be identified; the ELZ line is treated as contributing to the loss. No attachments.

event: During a maintenance course, Adv Nav aircraft VXE 954 was found with its FWAP set to the standard Block 30 vehicle type (95), reverting from 115 on every power cycle; fixed by reflashing the FWAP with the Adv Nav build.
component: FWAP firmware build (vehicle type 95 instead of 115)
failure_mode: FWAP loaded with the standard Block 30 build instead of the Adv Nav build, so vehicle type reverted to 95 at every power cycle
contributing: aircraft was connected to the same SGCS-253 as VXE 931, which had the same fault
possible manual vehicle type change in the gains panel (suspected, not confirmed)

evidence.quote: We updated the gains to 115 and sent to AP, but when we power cycle the aircraft the gains go back to 95 and will not stay as 115.
I have completed the XCOMM AP Firmware updated with the HEX file provided.  The throughput page in XCOMM is showing vehicle type 115.
Looks like it was connected to the same SGCS as 931.  Same 3 build times also.
The GCS correctly blocks uploading the wrong software so it feels like something was manually done with the gains, but obviously we can’t know for certain.

would_settle_it.what: XCOMM event logs showing when and from which GCS the non Adv Nav FWAP image was flashed

reasoning: The vehicle type kept reverting to 95 after power cycles, which is what the wrong FWAP build would do, and reflashing the FWAP with the 115 hex file fixed it and the launch wizard ran clean. The related VXE 931 ticket shows the same fault was a non Adv Nav build flashed onto an Adv Nav aircraft. How the wrong build got loaded was never established.
notes: Same issue as VXEP-1914 (VXE 931); both linked to SGCS-253. Team's only closing text is the fix ("Updated XCOMM firmware."), not a cause.

event: VXE 1018 gave a VTOL laser range finder failed error at the shield pilot step of the launch wizard during a training flight and could not launch; the fault could not be reproduced later.
failure_mode: LRF check failed in the launch wizard, probably from the LRF being blocked (knee under the ADP or thick grass)
contributing: launching from thick grass

evidence.quote: The autopilot has detected that the VTOL laser range finder has failed.
We set up aircraft 1018 and completed the launch wizard twice today with no errors during the pitot calibration.
Can not reproduced, test flown serviceable with customer (MOLSON)

team_view_in_comments: the error could of been inducted by the members knee being under the ADP blocking the LRF or they were also launching from a thick grass area

would_settle_it.what: condition of the LRF window on the ADP
LRF range readings at the time of the error to show a blocked or failed sensor

reasoning: The LRF error appeared once; the aircraft then passed the launch wizard twice, passed with the aircraft tilted both ways, and was test flown with the customer without the error. The team's best explanation is a blocked LRF during the check (knee under the ADP or thick grass), which is a plausible abnormal input, not a part failure. No AAR from the event is attached to confirm it.
notes: A center wing from VXE-1017 was put on 1018 at the time and it launched; later tests on 1018 were clean, so no part was implicated. The test flight comment says "15 June" but the attached packs are dated 2026-07-15, likely a typo for July.

event: VXE 1015 aborted during the VTOL launch climb with a VTOL fault for GPS position uncertainty just above the threshold and landed safely, at a tree covered site near Shepherdsville KY.
failure_mode: position uncertainty slightly exceeded the launch abort threshold with fewer satellites tracked than normal, triggering the designed abort
contributing: trees around the launch site reducing satellites tracked (suspected)
abort threshold of 15, later raised to 30
software before 6.7.1

evidence.quote: it is aborting due to a position uncertainty just above the threshold.
The aircraft is tracking less satellites than I’d normally see, so wondering if it has to do with the location they are taking off.
The below thresholds have been changed from 15 to 30 in the VTOL webpage for aircraft 1015.

team_root_cause: Aborted due to position uncertainty. 6.7.1 should improve performance

would_settle_it.what: satellite count, signal strength and position uncertainty against the threshold at the abort

reasoning: The engineer who reviewed the logs found the abort was triggered by position uncertainty just above the threshold, with fewer satellites than normal. This is a designed abort on a degraded GPS input, so it is scored on GPS. The tree cover around the site is the suspected reason for the low satellite count, which is an inference, not shown directly.
notes: Same event pattern and same night as VXEP-1913 (VXE 1017). The aircraft was not flown after the threshold change before the ticket was closed on the 6.7.1 update.

component: FWAP firmware build (non Adv Nav 6.6.1 instead of Adv Nav)
failure_mode: FWAP flashed with the non advanced nav 6.6.1 build, so vehicle type reverted to 95
contributing: flashing appears to have come from SGCS1-253 (IP 10.0.253.51)
possible manual vehicle type change in the gains panel (suspected, not confirmed)
no GPS fix or time in the logs since September, hiding the flash date

evidence.quote: At some point after September it was somehow flashed with the non-advanced nav version of 6.6.1 software
I think the incident occurred in XC000101.T01 with the GCS at IP address: 10.0.253.51.

event: VXE 942 showed a VTOL GPS fault at about 2000 ft AGL in the climb on battery fixed wing flight, then link was lost immediately and the aircraft was never recovered.
contributing: earlier VTOL launch abort the same day
a link "blip" on the second flight attributed to an SGCS power surge

Neither the SGCS2 or SGCS1 radios displayed the aircraft node on the network.
No WDT’s and GPS looks good throughout both flights.
If Silvus dropped out and was not a result of the aircraft losing line of sight with SGCS, this would indicate complete power failure on the vehicle.
Aircraft crashed, never recovered.

would_settle_it.what: attitude of the aircraft just before link loss
